newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to use public funds to buy jusen land--paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan to use public funds to buy jusen land--paper.

text.p: The Japanese government plans to use additional public funds to buy collateralised land formally owned by failed "jusen" mortgage companies and other troubled financial firms, a major financial daily reported on Thursday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun quoted government sources as saying that the central and local governments would purchase real estate held by loan-collecting bodies.
The move would be designed to activate the sluggish property market and help dispose of the non-performing loans of the firms, it said.
The government would use the land to build homes for the elderly and for parks, the paper said.
The government is expected to allocate more than four trillion yen for the purchase of public land in 1997/98, starting on April 1, it said.
Government officials were not immediately available for comment on the report.
